questions.q: What does the story of early trains limited to 30 mph illustrate?
a: What is possible is often limited only by how much we try
Technology always advances faster than safety rules
People resist new inventions out of envy
Progress depends mainly on government funding
questions.why: Lesson 1 uses the belief that passengers would explode above 30 mph to show that our sense of what is possible is often self-imposed.

questions.q: What did Roger Bannister's four-minute mile show, according to the summary?
a: A believed limit falls once someone proves it can be done
Natural talent matters far more than consistent training
Athletic records are mostly a matter of luck
The human body has a fixed ceiling that cannot move
questions.why: Lesson 1 notes that the mile was thought impossible until Bannister ran it, after which others quickly followed.

questions.q: What is an upper limit mindset, as Hendricks describes it?
a: A subconscious cap that makes us sabotage ourselves when things go well
A habit of setting goals that are far too ambitious
A belief that hard work always pays off in the end
A tendency to compare ourselves with more successful people
questions.why: Lesson 2 explains that we carry a subconscious idea of how much happiness we deserve, so we create fake drama when life goes too well.

questions.q: How does Hendricks suggest you deal with fear?
a: Breathe into it slowly and deeply
Avoid the situation until the fear fades
Talk yourself out of feeling afraid
Replace the fear with controlled anger
questions.why: Lesson 2 quotes the idea that fear is excitement without breath, and recommends slow, deep breathing to turn stress into energy.

questions.q: In Hendricks's four work zones, what defines the Zone of Genius?
a: You are the best in the world at that task
You are highly skilled and few people can match you
You are competent enough to keep the job
You are doing work that feels easy and comfortable
questions.why: Lesson 3 ranks the zones from incompetence to genius, and says the Zone of Genius is where you are literally the best in the world.
